evals.prompt: Help me create a new skill, including frontmatter, references, eval files, and validation guidance.
evals.expected_behavior: The response explains the standard skill shape, frontmatter, progressive disclosure, eval schemas, no-script-by-default guidance, and offers a concrete starter scaffold with target-skill validation guidance.
assertions: Mentions frontmatter and when-to-use descriptions.
Mentions references or evals and progressive disclosure.
Mentions scripts as selective rather than default.
Points to or provides a starter scaffold with SKILL.md, references, and eval files.
Separates catalog-wide validation from target-skill eval commands.
Uses the new skill path rather than hardcoded skill-creator eval paths when describing validation.

evals.prompt: Draft frontmatter and the Use this skill when / Do not use this skill when sections for a brand-new `cloudflare-d1-migrations`-adjacent skill about D1 query tuning.
evals.expected_behavior: Before drafting, checks skills/README.md and nearby skills (cloudflare-d1-migrations, repository-adapters) to establish the boundary, consults assets/skill-template.md for the canonical outline and references/catalog-standard.md for the frontmatter spec, then writes trigger language (description, Use/Do-not-use) before any workflow or support-file content.
assertions: Checks skills/README.md or nearby skills for boundary overlap before drafting the new skill's content
Uses assets/skill-template.md's canonical outline and references/catalog-standard.md's frontmatter spec rather than inventing a new structure
Writes the frontmatter description plus Use this skill when / Do not use this skill when before workflow or support-file content
Produces a description that states both when to use it and, given the overlap with cloudflare-d1-query-tuning, when not to

evals.prompt: Update an existing skill so it has better metadata, examples, and trigger coverage.
evals.expected_behavior: The response covers frontmatter metadata, example coverage, trigger and anti-trigger wording, evals, validation tooling, and iteration based on real execution.
assertions: Mentions metadata or versioning.
Mentions examples in SKILL.md or representative prompts in support files.
Mentions trigger wording or anti-triggers.
Mentions evals and validation tooling.
Mentions iterative improvement using real tasks.

evals.prompt: This new skill is just a short workflow with two examples — do I need references/, evals/, scripts/, and assets/ folders too?
evals.expected_behavior: Recommends the minimal useful package for the described scope: keep the short workflow in SKILL.md, skip references/evals/scripts/assets unless they clearly add value, and explicitly avoid adding scripts/ or empty scaffolding just to match the directory pattern.
assertions: Does not recommend adding scripts/ by default for a simple two-example workflow
Explicitly says to skip support directories that would not add real signal here
Frames the decision as choosing the minimal useful package, not the full starter bundle unconditionally
Does not instruct creating empty or placeholder scaffolding files

evals.prompt: I have reusable workflow guidance. Should this be a skill, instructions, an agent, or an extension?
evals.expected_behavior: The response compares nearby customization surfaces before assuming the answer is a skill and recommends the minimal useful package when a skill is appropriate.
assertions: Compares the skill option against at least one nearby surface such as instructions, agents, extensions, or MCP.
Mentions deciding whether the guidance belongs in a skill before drafting content.
Mentions keeping the package minimal unless references, evals, scripts, or assets clearly add value.

evals.prompt: This guidance should just always apply to every task in the repo, no matter what the user asks. Make it a skill.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from creating a skill because guidance that should always apply belongs in repository instruction files (AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md) rather than a skill package that has to be selected/triggered.
assertions: Does not scaffold a new skill package for always-apply guidance
Points toward repository instruction files or agent-instructions instead
Explains that skills are selected/triggered per-task, which conflicts with an always-apply requirement
deterministic_checks: does not create a skills/<name>/SKILL.md for this request

evals.prompt: I need a named specialist persona — call it 'PR Reviewer Bot' — with its own voice and role for reviewing PRs. Package it as a skill.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from skill-creator's skill packaging because a named specialist role belongs in agents/, not skills/, per this skill's own Do not use this skill when list.
assertions: Does not scaffold a skills/<name>/SKILL.md package for a named specialist persona
States that named specialist roles belong under agents/ instead
